doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Return to New York in the late 1960s
title: Playing for Sonny Rollins' TV documentary
summary: Rollins pays Ware to appear with him in an English TV documentary which he never sees in full.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: However, right after that, Sonny Rollins Robbins (PHONETIC) called me. He was doing a -- they was doing a TV documentary about him and the bridge where, you know, he was out playing, but he hadn't come back into the clubs, whatever. But it was an English TV company and so he says, 'Just come over to the house, Wilbur, and I'll pay you X-amount of dollars just to make this with me, just you and I, and we'll talk, what have you.' It was a nice little taste of money just to do that, although I never saw the --
-- the show. You know, I never saw it.
Uh-uh. They showed parts of it on American Public Broadcasting TV. I saw that. But I didn't see myself in it.
Showed him down in the subway, just with his horn out.
The part I was in, that was up in his apartment, just he and I. We didn't play no tunes or nothing. He would just run over his horn and I'd pull a few notes. But we got paid for it.
